messages.subject: Working with arrays and simmer
parts:
Hi,

First of all, congrats for the great package! From what I've seen, it has a lot of useful and standard tools for DES. Having this open-source option is a great deal!

Anyway, I've been trying to model an inventory system with simmer by using a trajectory as a general definition for any demand arrival, irrespective of the place where demand arrives, so I need to keep track of the inventory in many "locations" using one single trajectory. For that I was thinking on using an array (in this case a matrix) that keeps track of every inventory position, depending on the location where the demand arrived. The issue is that I haven't been able to change the value of an "external" array by calling an "external" function, as it seems that the simulation does not interact with these external definitions.

I've seen that simmer allows to set a global variable for the simulation, but this variable is only numeric and it cannot work as an array/matrix. I need to use an array/matrix because I want the simulation to be flexible so I can use one single trajectory to define the same tasks but with different "locations"; otherwise, if I have, for example, a 100 location network, then I would need to define 100 different trajectories and/or global variables. Does anyone have any idea how can I accomplish this?

The code is this, in case you want to have an idea of what I'm trying to accomplish, the idea is that the on-hand inventory "onhand[1,1]" should consume inventory every period, depending on the demand, so that at the last periods there are some backorders accumulated.

onhand <- matrix(nrow=100,ncol=100)
backorders <- matrix(nrow=100,ncol=100)
for(i in 1:5)
{
  onhand[1,i] <- 100
  backorders[1,i] <- 0
}

temp1 <- function(a,b)
{
  if (onhand[1,a]>b)
  {
    onhand[1,a]<-onhand[1,a]-b
  }
  else
  {
    backorders[1,a]<-b-onhand[1,a]
    onhand[1,a]<-0
  }
  return(paste(a,b,onhand[1,a],backorders[1,a]))
}

sim <- simmer()

arrival <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute("demand",function() rnorm(1,50,10)) %>%
  set_attribute("element", 1) %>%
  log_(function() (temp1(get_attribute(sim,"element"),get_attribute(sim,"demand"))))

  sim <- simmer("sim") %>%
  add_generator("arrival", arrival, function() 1)

sim %>% run(until=5)

On Tue, 16 Jul 2019 at 10:53, Rodrigo Romero Silva <rrom...@up.edu.mx> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> First of all, congrats for the great package! From what I've seen, it has a lot of useful and standard tools for DES. Having this open-source option is a great deal!

> Anyway, I've been trying to model an inventory system with simmer by using a trajectory as a general definition for any demand arrival, irrespective of the place where demand arrives, so I need to keep track of the inventory in many "locations" using one single trajectory. For that I was thinking on using an array (in this case a matrix) that keeps track of every inventory position, depending on the location where the demand arrived. The issue is that I haven't been able to change the value of an "external" array by calling an "external" function, as it seems that the simulation does not interact with these external definitions.
>
> I've seen that simmer allows to set a global variable for the simulation, but this variable is only numeric and it cannot work as an array/matrix. I need to use an array/matrix because I want the simulation to be flexible so I can use one single trajectory to define the same tasks but with different "locations"; otherwise, if I have, for example, a 100 location network, then I would need to define 100 different trajectories and/or global variables. Does anyone have any idea how can I accomplish this?

In short, use <<- instead of <-.

Long explanation follows. When you use a variable, there's a search
through parent environments until there's a match (in your case, in
the global environment). Instead, when you try to change a variable,
operators <- and = assign into the environment in which they are
evaluated. This means that, regardless there's a variable with the
same name in the global environment, a new one is created locally. You
need to use <<- to force that same search across environment
boundaries and modify the global one.

Iñaki
